newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Cochin Refineries seeks partner.
newsitem.headline: India's Cochin Refineries seeks partner.

text.p: Indian state-run oil refiner Cochin Refineries Ltd said on Monday that it is looking for a partner to take a 26 percent stake in a 500 megawatt power plant it plans to set up in the southern state of Kerala.

The company said in an advertisement in the Business Standard newspaper that any Indian or foreign firms could apply provided they agreed to take a 26 percent stake in the power project, the same size as Cochin Refineries' holding.
The partner also has to agree that the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), which will buy all of the power generated by the plant, will take an 11 percent stake, it said.
The power plant in Ambalamugal, Kerala, will be refinery residue based, and will be set up next to Cochin's existing refinery.
The qualification document will be available on Tuesday, and the deadline for applying to become the joint venture partner is July 21.
The notice said that the power project has in principle been cleared by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA).
